overview: After 1.d4 d5 2.c4 Black plays 2...b5, offering a wing pawn. After 3.cxb5 White has an extra pawn; Black hopes for quick development with ...Nf6 and ...c6, opening lines against the White queenside. Against sensible play White keeps the pawn and a solid position.

white_ideas.idea: Take with cxb5 and keep the pawn
Develop with Nc3, Nf3 and e3

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...Nf6 and ...c6, hitting the b5 pawn

typical_structures.structure: White extra pawn on b5 or a-file

character.notes: A dubious gambit where Black gets some pressure but little else.

gambit.notes: White can take on b5 and keep the pawn with sensible play.

structure.notes: Semi-open with the c-file and b-file in play.

approach.notes: Almost never played by strong players.

character.reason: Black is a pawn down and must play actively for the compensation.

gambit.reason: Black offers the b-pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.reason: Black does not have enough for the pawn.

structure.reason: The c-file and b-file open while the centre stays semi-open.

approach.reason: Hardly ever chosen by strong players.

level.reason: A dubious line cannot be Beginner.

plans.reason: Black pays a pawn for time.
